# Discovery in Practice

> Practical explanations of microplate assays, detection technology, instruments and drug discovery.

Canonical HTML pages are the citation targets. The Markdown and JSON links provide synchronized article renditions, with author, publication and update dates, references, license and content hashes. Original articles are CC BY 4.0; search, retrieval and AI training are welcome. Third-party sources retain their licenses. Illustrative calculations are not raw experimental measurements.

## Library sections

- [Reference library](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/): All published articles grouped by question.
- [Assays](https://discoveryinpractice.com/assays/): Choose a microplate assay for the biological event you want to measure, then work through its detection chemistry, controls and interpretation.
- [Result interpretation](https://discoveryinpractice.com/troubleshooting/): Explore what microplate assay signals reveal about your experiment, from background and variability to plate handling and detection effects.
- [Concepts](https://discoveryinpractice.com/concepts/): Understand how microplate readers measure light and how detector response, photon statistics and ratio calculations shape the numbers you report.
- [Comparisons](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/): Compare assay formats and screening equipment by the measurement you need, the controls it requires and the practical trade-offs.

## Assays — authoritative Markdown

- [ADP-Glo: the light comes after the kinase](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/adp-glo-light-after-kinase/article.md): ADP-Glo light is the endpoint of a multistep detection sequence, so a lower signal can arise outside the kinase reaction. This article shows how to reconstruct the endpoint with ATP/ADP controls and interpret temperature, timing, conversion, and ATP-dependent potency.
- [CellTiter-Glo: when less light doesn’t mean fewer cells](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/celltiter-glo-light-cells/article.md): CellTiter-Glo measures ATP-dependent light, not cell number directly, so metabolism and detection conditions can change the signal independently of abundance. The article separates biological effects from reagent, temperature, mixing, and detector effects and proposes controls for each.
- [HiBiT: did the protein disappear, or just the light?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/hibit-protein-or-light/article.md): A decrease in HiBiT light can reflect less tagged protein or a change in complementation, luciferase activity, lysis, background, or measurement. The article separates reporter abundance from accelerated degradation and outlines controls that test the detection system and native protein.
- [Lumit: no wash steps doesn't mean no interference](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/lumit-interference-controls/article.md): Investigate Lumit results with dilution series, matrix controls and tests that separate antibody recognition, light production and detector response.
- [Let the reaction and the detector use different concentrations](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/kinase-assay-reaction-detection-dilution/article.md): Optimize kinase reactions and detection separately. Follow a worked dilution example, account for total substrate and validate stopping, timing and temperature.
- [HTRF: the ratio is not the whole result](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/htrf-ratio-whole-result/article.md): A stable HTRF ratio can conceal a major loss of signal, degraded precision, or a channel-specific interference. The article explains how to retain and interpret both emission channels, per-well ratios, and acquisition conditions.
- [Your fluorescent label is part of the experiment](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/choosing-fluorescence-polarization-tracer/article.md): Choose a fluorescence polarization tracer by matching lifetime to molecular motion, testing the conjugate and checking controls in the actual assay matrix.
- [One extra carbon can change the binding result](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-polarization-tracer-linker-length/article.md): A one-carbon linker change can alter tracer affinity and assay performance. Learn how to separate binding chemistry from your fluorescence polarization window.
- [Waiting longer can move the competition curve](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/incubation-time-competition-assay-ic50/article.md): Longer incubation can improve an assay window while changing potency. Explore AlphaScreen and hERG examples and a practical way to qualify complete curves.
- [NanoBRET: proximity needs a good alibi](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/nanobret-assay-optimization-dual-emission/article.md): Improve NanoBRET assays with expression controls, simultaneous dual-emission detection, linearity checks and stable temperature. Includes worked examples.
- [How should I optimize NanoBRET donor and acceptor filters?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/optimize-nanobret-donor-acceptor-filters/article.md): Choose assay-specific NanoBRET emission filters using raw channels, negative controls, ratio precision and simultaneous dual-emission detection.
- [1536-well assays: the waiting time is part of the assay](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/1536-well-assay-evaporation-temperature/article.md): Optimize 1536-well assays for real screening runs: control evaporation, queue time, mixing, room-temperature glow detection and plate reader stability.
- [Choosing a microplate: the plastic is part of the assay](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/choosing-microplates-surface-color-crosstalk/article.md): Choose microplates by surface, color, geometry and working volume. Use practical tests to separate useful signal from adsorption, crosstalk and evaporation.
- [Should I read a cell-based luminescence assay at 37°C or at room temperature?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/cell-luminescence-37c-room-temperature/article.md): Choose detection temperature using CellTiter-Glo, RealTime-Glo MT and HiBiT Lytic protocols, with clear distinctions between live-cell and lytic assays.
- [When do I need inject-and-read measurements instead of dispensing the whole plate first?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/when-to-use-inject-and-read/article.md): Choose inject-and-read from reaction kinetics and timing tolerance, with examples distinguishing fast signals from stable glow endpoints.

## Result interpretation — authoritative Markdown

- [Why do I get negative fluorescence or luminescence values after blank subtraction?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/negative-values-blank-subtraction/article.md): Understand negative fluorescence or luminescence after blank subtraction, diagnose blank mismatch and avoid bias from replacing negatives with zero.
- [Why does subtracting background make my CV worse?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/background-subtraction-increases-cv/article.md): Learn why blank subtraction raises CV, how shared blanks create correlated uncertainty and why optical background prevention helps.
- [Why does my HTRF assay still have high background after I increase the delay time?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/htrf-high-background-delay-time/article.md): Troubleshoot persistent HTRF background with donor-only, acceptor-only and assay controls before changing delay, filters or integration time.
- [AlphaPlex: your first measurement can change the second](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/alphaplex-dual-emission-crosstalk/article.md): Learn why AlphaPlex read order matters, how simultaneous dual emission helps, and how to distinguish spectral leakage, well crosstalk and antibody effects.
- [Why can my NanoBRET ratio stay constant while the donor signal falls?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/nanobret-ratio-constant-donor-signal-falls/article.md): Why a NanoBRET ratio can stay constant as donor light falls, how precision suffers and which raw signals and controls to inspect.
- [Why does the mP value of my free FP tracer change when I change its concentration?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/free-fp-tracer-concentration-mp/article.md): Diagnose concentration-dependent fluorescence polarization using raw channels, matched blanks, linearity checks and controls for tracer behavior.
- [Can I reuse the same FP G factor after changing filters, gain settings or readers?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/reuse-fp-g-factor-filters-gain-reader/article.md): Know when to verify or recalibrate an FP G factor after changing filters, gains or readers, and why one matching reference value is insufficient.
- [Can sequential AlphaPlex channel reads bias the result even if both channels look stable?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/sequential-alphaplex-channel-bias/article.md): See how AlphaPlex channel order can bias a repeatable ratio, and how simultaneous dual emission and matched reading-history controls help.
- [Why are repeated readings of one well precise while replicate wells disagree?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/repeat-reads-versus-replicate-wells/article.md): Separate reader repeatability from dispensing, cell loading, position effects and preparation variability using a staged comparison.
- [Why does an HTRF assay have good signal-to-background but poor Z-prime?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/htrf-good-signal-background-low-z-prime/article.md): Explain low HTRF Z-prime despite a good signal window using control variability, raw donor and acceptor data, and a worked example.
- [Why does my assay have low Z-prime after moving from 384 to 1536 wells?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/low-z-prime-384-to-1536-wells/article.md): Diagnose low Z-prime after miniaturizing from 384 to 1536 wells, including photon counts, cell loading, evaporation and read geometry.
- [Read the plate map before you read the statistic](https://discoveryinpractice.com/bench-tips/plate-map/article.md): Inspect spatial patterns alongside control statistics, then use those patterns to choose a follow-up check.
- [The plate is recording its temperature history](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/microplate-temperature-stability-qualification/article.md): Qualify liquid temperature during plate reads, busy runs and interruptions. Separate thermal drift from evaporation and optical crosstalk before correcting data.
- [Dispensed does not mean mixed](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/microplate-mixing-dispensing-1536-well/article.md): Accurate dispensing can still create uneven early exposure. Explore DMSO gradients, diffusion times and practical mixing checks for 384- and 1536-well assays.
- [The plate queue changed your IC50](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/plate-queue-ic50-assay-timing/article.md): Map assay clocks, challenge plate queues and define restart rules. Use full curves, temperature control and reliable detection to test a screening workflow.
- [Your Alpha assay is also a thermometer](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/alpha-assay-temperature/article.md): Troubleshoot temperature effects in Alpha assays by testing liquid temperature, plate timing and control behavior under realistic screening conditions.
- [Why does my plate reader warm the plate when incubation is switched off?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/plate-reader-warming-incubation-off/article.md): Understand plate-reader warming, room-temperature chamber control and practical temperature checks for CellTiter-Glo and Alpha assays.
- [Can a reader specified as “ambient +4°C” keep my assay at room temperature?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/ambient-plus-four-room-temperature-plate-reader/article.md): Understand above-ambient temperature specifications, chamber heating and cooling, and the checks needed for stable room-temperature assay detection.
- [How can I tell whether the liquid in my plate has reached the reader's temperature setpoint?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/plate-liquid-temperature-reader-setpoint/article.md): Distinguish chamber and liquid temperatures, understand thermal lag, and qualify equilibration across wells during a realistic plate-reader run.
- [Why do Alpha or glow-luminescence controls drift from the first plate to the last?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/alpha-glow-luminescence-controls-drift/article.md): Separate assay age, reagent changes and temperature drift when Alpha or glow-luminescence controls change from the first plate to the last.
- [What causes a plate edge effect: evaporation, temperature or cell biology?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/plate-edge-effect-evaporation-temperature-cells/article.md): Diagnose microplate edge effects with volume, temperature and cell-distribution checks before applying corrections or changing the assay workflow.
- [How do I know whether a 384- or 1536-well assay is actually mixed?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/384-1536-well-assay-mixing/article.md): Learn why shaking speed and stable fluorescence do not prove mixing, and how to qualify a mixing method for a dense microplate assay.
- [Can a plate lid or sealing film change my fluorescence, luminescence or absorbance results?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/plate-lid-sealing-film-reader-results/article.md): Check transmission, fluorescence, condensation and read geometry before using a lid or sealing film during microplate measurements.
- [How do I test for injector carryover in a plate reader?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/test-plate-reader-injector-carryover/article.md): Test injector carryover with sequential blanks and positive-control recovery, including residues that suppress rather than increase luminescence.
- [Why is my luminescence signal lower on one plate reader than another?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/luminescence-signal-different-plate-readers/article.md): Learn why luminescence signals differ between readers and how to compare precision, linearity, temperature and crosstalk fairly.
- [TR-FRET: waiting doesn’t fix the wrong photons](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/tr-fret-troubleshooting-filters-timing-excitation/article.md): Troubleshoot HTRF and LanthaScreen assays by separating timing from spectral leakage. Learn when filters, excitation and reader controls improve results.
- [How much does read height matter in fluorescence intensity?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-intensity-read-height/article.md): Optimize fluorescence read height using blanks and weak samples, with practical checks for plate geometry, fill volume and top versus bottom reads.
- [What causes crosstalk in 384- and 1536-well plates?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/crosstalk-384-1536-well-plates/article.md): Find the optical causes of microplate crosstalk, test bright-neighbor interference and distinguish leakage from sample carryover.
- [Why can increasing PMT gain make low-signal fluorescence CV worse?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/pmt-gain-low-signal-fluorescence-cv/article.md): Why higher PMT gain can leave fluorescence precision unchanged or make it worse, with blank checks, gain tests and practical interpretation.
- [When does a wider fluorescence bandwidth improve sensitivity—and when does it make results worse?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-bandwidth-sensitivity/article.md): Learn when wider fluorescence bandwidth improves sensitivity, when it adds background and how to compare settings using weak samples and blanks.
- [Should I always read at a fluorophore's published excitation and emission peaks?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-excitation-emission-wavelengths/article.md): Why published dye peaks are starting points, with FITC wavelengths, bandwidth overlap and practical tests using low positives and realistic blanks.
- [Top vs bottom read: which should I use for cell-based fluorescence?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/top-vs-bottom-read-cell-fluorescence/article.md): Choose top or bottom plate reading using cell location, medium background, plate transmission and matched controls while preserving assay biology.
- [Why can a white plate outperform a black plate in a TR-FRET assay?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/white-vs-black-plates-tr-fret-htrf/article.md): Compare white and black TR-FRET plates through photon statistics, laser excitation, detector efficiency, crosstalk and assay-specific requirements.
- [Why can crosstalk correction fix the mean but leave weak wells unreliable?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/crosstalk-correction-weak-well-noise/article.md): See why subtracting crosstalk can correct a mean while leaving photon noise, and how to test optical suppression and correction independently.
- [When does laser excitation improve an HTRF or TR-FRET assay?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/laser-excitation-htrf-tr-fret/article.md): When laser excitation improves HTRF and TR-FRET precision or speed, with donor compatibility, paired detection and a practical comparison plan.
- [When blocking luciferase creates more light](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/luciferase-inhibitor-increased-signal/article.md): Why a luciferase inhibitor can make cells brighter, how reporter stabilization changes the result, and which controls separate protein abundance from activity.
- [The sample got brighter when we diluted it](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/alpha-assay-hook-effect-dilution/article.md): A weak Alpha signal can hide excess analyte. Learn to interpret dilution series and separate the hook effect from matrix interference and detector compression.
- [The inactive ingredient in the reagent bottle](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/alpha-assay-azide-biotin-buffer-interference/article.md): Trace azide, free biotin and medium carryover into Alpha assays. Learn how dilution and addition order change interference and the controls needed to find it.
- [The inhibitor that made the reporter brighter](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/luciferase-reporter-hit-confirmation/article.md): Investigate brighter luciferase reporter hits with raw-channel checks, reporter counterscreens and independent endpoints that can retain useful biology.
- [Why does my sample get brighter when I dilute it?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-increases-after-dilution/article.md): Distinguish raw fluorescence from dilution-corrected recovery, then investigate inner-filter effects, antigen excess, matrix interference and overload.
- [Why does rereading an Alpha assay change its signal?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/rereading-alpha-assay-signal-change/article.md): Separate Alpha signal changes caused by reaction age, temperature and excitation history, with a matched once-read versus reread experiment.
- [How can I tell whether a fluorescent screening hit is active or just interfering with detection?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescent-screening-hit-interference/article.md): Separate real activity from autofluorescence, quenching and inner-filter effects with compound-only controls and matched detection counterassays.
- [How can I tell whether a luminescence hit changes the biology or inhibits the reporter reaction?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/luminescence-hit-reporter-inhibition/article.md): Test luminescence hits for reporter inhibition, signal quenching and reporter stabilization using matched counterassays and independent biology.

## Concepts — authoritative Markdown

- [What is the difference between analog and photon-counting luminescence detection?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/analog-photon-counting-luminescence/article.md): Compare analog and photon-counting readout, understand why longer integration cannot fix pulse overlap and qualify a useful linear range.
- [Can PMT saturation or signal compression occur without an overload warning?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/pmt-saturation-signal-compression-no-warning/article.md): Learn how luminescence signal compression can precede an overload warning, distort results and appear in a practical detector-linearity check.
- [A better Z′ can hide a worse measurement](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/z-prime-detector-linearity/article.md): A higher Z′ can reflect nonlinear detector compression rather than a better assay. This article explains how bright-well variation can shrink while effect sizes become distorted, and how to check proportionality without confusing detector behavior with assay chemistry.
- [Controls can look better when the detector stops telling the truth](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/z-prime-linearity-screen-qualification/article.md): Tight controls can conceal signal compression. Qualify intermediate responses, optical linearity, crosstalk and temperature before accepting a screening window.
- [Should I use automatic gain on every plate in a screening run?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/automatic-gain-screening-plates/article.md): When to keep plate reader gain fixed, when calibrated automatic range selection helps and how to check comparability across a screening run.
- [Why do filter and monochromator readers perform differently at the same nominal wavelengths?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/filter-monochromator-same-wavelengths/article.md): Why matching wavelengths does not match plate reader performance, with bandwidth, blocking, dichroics and practical method-transfer checks.
- [What does a dichroic mirror change in a fluorescence measurement?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/dichroic-mirror-fluorescence-plate-reader/article.md): How dichroic mirrors improve fluorescence light collection and excitation rejection, including monochromator optics and practical background checks.
- [What does a dedicated TR-FRET detector add beyond time-gating a general-purpose PMT?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/dedicated-tr-fret-detector-time-gating/article.md): Understand detector recovery, delayed background, spectral sensitivity and linearity when evaluating dedicated TR-FRET detection and laser excitation.
- [When does reading longer stop improving assay CV?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/luminescence-integration-time/article.md): Longer luminescence reads help when photon collection limits precision, but they cannot remove persistent differences between wells. This article shows how to compare repeated reads with independently prepared replicates, account for background noise, and choose a useful stopping point.
- [Why do my bright controls have excellent CVs while my weak samples are unreliable?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/bright-control-cv-weak-samples/article.md): Why bright controls can have excellent CV while weak samples remain unreliable, with photon statistics, background and working-range checks.
- [The ratio survived but the precision did not](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fp-ratio-photon-loss-precision/article.md): An unchanged FP ratio can hide lost precision. Follow photon-count examples and practical controls for attenuation, background and fluorescent compounds.
- [Your fluorescence polarization result is hiding two measurements](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fp-two-measurements/article.md): A fluorescence-polarization value is calculated from parallel and perpendicular intensity measurements, and the ratio can hide low photon counts or timing mismatch. The article explains how to preserve both channels, interpret intensity and binding curves, and qualify tracer and reader behavior.
- [Half the molecules and two thirds of the light](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/fluorescence-polarization-brightness-correction-kd/article.md): Binding can change tracer brightness and shift an apparent Kd while the curve still fits beautifully. See the equations, controls and fluorescence data to keep.
- [More receptor can make affinity harder to measure](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/ligand-depletion-receptor-concentration/article.md): See how receptor concentration changes free ligand, shifts binding midpoints and limits Kd estimates, with worked examples and practical assay controls.
- [When does simultaneous dual-emission detection improve FP, TR-FRET or BRET precision?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/simultaneous-dual-emission-ratio-precision/article.md): How simultaneous dual-emission detection reduces timing errors in FP, TR-FRET and BRET, and why weak channels and calibration still matter.
- [Are two PMTs enough for accurate ratiometric measurements, or do they need matching and calibration?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/matched-pmts-ratio-calibration/article.md): Learn why simultaneous detection, relative channel calibration and linearity all matter for accurate FP, TR-FRET and BRET measurements.
- [Why does absorbance change when I change the volume, even at the same concentration?](https://discoveryinpractice.com/articles/microplate-absorbance-volume-pathlength/article.md): Understand why constant-concentration samples give different absorbance at different volumes, and when pathlength correction can help.

## Comparisons — authoritative Markdown

- [Microplate kinase assays: choose the event you need to measure](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/microplate-kinase-assays/article.md): ADP production, ATP depletion, substrate phosphorylation and target binding are useful measurements. They are not interchangeable evidence of kinase inhibition.
- [DNA quantification: five methods, five different answers](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/dna-quantification/article.md): DNA mass, target copies, amplifiable library molecules and fragment integrity are different measurements. Choose the answer your next experiment needs before choosing the instrument.
- [Choosing Alpha HTRF and alternative screening assays](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/alpha-htrf-fp-lumit-assay-comparison/article.md): Match the assay to the molecular event and the interference you can control
- [Choosing assays for molecular glue and PROTAC screening](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/protac-molecular-glue-bretsa-cetsa-nanobret-assays/article.md): Separate cellular engagement recruitment ubiquitination and protein loss
- [Choosing MSD Luminex and alternative biomarker assays](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/msd-luminex-biomarker-assays/article.md): Select the panel that can quantify the biology in your actual samples
- [Automated confocal screening: compare the result, not the camera speed](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/confocal-screening-systems/article.md): Six representative high-content imaging families compared by optics, simultaneous channels, live-cell conditions and the work required to turn a plate into reliable measurements.
- [Label free binding instruments for drug discovery](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/label-free-binding-instruments/article.md): Comparing SPR BLI and GCI for affinity kinetics and screening
- [Low volume liquid handling for drug discovery](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/low-volume-liquid-handling/article.md): Choosing among acoustic transfer digital dispensing and positive displacement
- [Flow cytometers for drug discovery screening](https://discoveryinpractice.com/compare/screening-flow-cytometers/article.md): Comparing iQue CytoFLEX and Attune plate based workflows
